issues.theCaveat: STATED RATHER THAN OMITTED, because it is the strongest thing that can be said against the row. A member who voted yea will say the vote PROTECTS public schools by removing a hostile foreign government from them, and that reading is not silly — it is the bill's motive, and it is why the sponsors named it the PROTECT Our Kids Act. It is not the reading the key takes, for the reason public_schools' own scope note gives in the sentence quoted above: the mapping reads the operative funding effect and refuses to dress a withdrawal of funds as a reform. The direct precedent is already live and already decided the same way — 2026 S.B. 321's graduated phase-out of hold harmless on voted and board levies is filed yea_opposes on this key, over exactly the same objection that its sponsors called it a formula modernisation. Reading H.R. 1069 the other way would require reading motive over text on a key whose scope note forbids it, and would put this bill on the opposite side of the axis from a state bill that does the same thing. The motive is not lost to the reader: it is in the bill's short title, which is what the pack displays beside the row.

Sec. 2(a) is the bill's only operative provision, and it reaches every ED programme through its cross-reference to 20 U.S.C. 1221(c)(1); Sec. 2(b) is an effective date, Sec. 2(c) a waiver for pre-enactment contracts, and Sec. 2(d) a 90-day notice to state educational agencies. public_schools' scope note is 'the money and staffing of the DISTRICT system — funding formulas, teacher compensation, levy protection, and duties the state imposes on and resources through local education agencies', and its chip is 'Raise teacher pay and fund public schools and classrooms'. A federal funding condition on local education agencies is that axis one level up, and it is the only axis in the vocabulary the bill's operative text touches. The polarity follows the key's own published polarity rule — 'oppose = it withdrew a funding protection, and the mapping says so rather than dressing a cut as a reform' — so yea_opposes; Congress's own long title states the effect in the same direction, 'To prohibit the availability of Federal education funds for elementary and secondary schools that receive direct or indirect support from the Government of the People's Republic of China.' A member who voted yea will say the vote protects public schools by removing a hostile foreign government from them: that is the bill's motive, it is why the sponsors named it the PROTECT Our Kids Act, and it is displayed beside this row in the bill's short title — but the key reads the operative funding effect, exactly as Utah 2026 S.B. 321's hold-harmless phase-out is filed yea_opposes here over the identical objection. PRIMARY, because the funding prohibition is the bill's only operative provision. Weight 90 rather than 100 follows the sibling precedent H.R. 1005 in this same Congress, which carries gov_transparency at 90 primary on the same shape: the operative axis is the whole mechanism, but the bill's named subject — PRC influence in schools — sits outside the vocabulary, and 100 is reserved in this corpus for a measure whose own subject IS the key. This is the record's first federal public_schools PRIMARY in either chamber; the only other federal rows on the key are package-borne secondaries on H.R. 1319 (w50), S. 2938 (w45) and H.R. 28 (w55), which is why 85 House members read the axis off a vehicle rather than off their own vote. issues.why: REFUSED on the text, and this is the closest call among the four. gov_transparency's chip is 'Force more disclosure, ban member stock trading and toughen ethics rules', and the sibling bill H.R. 1005 — same Congress, same rule (H.Res. 916), same PRC-in-K-12 subject — carries it at 90 primary because H.R. 1005 REQUIRES schools to disclose foreign-source funds. H.R. 1069 compels no disclosure. Its only publication requirement is inside Sec. 2(c), the waiver: a school that wants to keep a pre-enactment contract must publish the unredacted text and a benefit statement. That is a condition on an exemption a school may decline to seek, not a disclosure duty the bill imposes; a school with no pre-enactment contract publishes nothing, and a school that gives up the contract publishes nothing. Filing gov_transparency off an opt-in waiver clause would read a transparency record onto 109 members for a duty the bill does not place on anyone.

REFUSED on keyword reach. strong_defense's keyword list contains 'china' and 'adversaries', and that is the entire case for the mapping. Its chip is 'Maintain the strongest military and stand firm abroad' and F4's scope note routes what the armed forces are authorised, funded and equipped to do — the NDAAs, end strengths, procurement — to this key. H.R. 1069 authorises nothing, funds nothing and equips nothing; it is a condition on Title I-style grants to school districts. If a bill counts as a defence act because the word 'china' appears in its findings, then every appropriations rider is a defence act, and the key stops meaning anything for the 109 members who hold it.

REFUSED on the text, and the refusal is written out because the corpus's own treatment of a near neighbour cuts the other way and a reader is entitled to know why. H.R. 1049, the Transparency in Reporting of Adversarial Contributions to Education Act, is mapped edu_parental at 100 primary plus gov_transparency at 65 — same Congress, same rule, same adversarial-funding-in-education family. edu_parental's chip is 'Give parents more say over curriculum, library materials and what their children are taught'. H.R. 1049 earns it because its operative provision puts information about adversarial contributions in front of the public, which is something a parent can act on. H.R. 1069 has no parent-facing provision at all: no notice to parents, no curriculum review, no opt-out, no consent. Its single notification requirement, Sec. 2(d), runs from the Secretary to STATE EDUCATIONAL AGENCIES. Nothing in the engrossed text mentions a parent, a curriculum, a library or an instructional material. The neighbour is mapped differently because the neighbour's text is different.

issues.why: REFUSED — REVERSAL OF A STANDING WRITTEN REFUSAL, DECLINED. This row was drafted, argued from the engrossed text, measured, and it is NOT SHIPPED, because the runbook refuses it by name and predicts, exactly, the effect this wave went on to measure. db/vr-ingest-runbook.md rule 3: "gov_regulation is about the regulatory question, not about every mandate. Reserve it for measures whose primary operative purpose is regulation itself: CRA disapprovals, regulatory-budget caps, red-tape hotlines, rulemaking-quality bills. Do not map a measure to it merely because the measure directs an agency to issue or enforce a rule — that description fits most of the statute book, and it would turn a member's deregulation stance into a contradiction on any safety vote. This is why H.R. 973 (CPSC rule for micromobility batteries) and S. 2503 (ADS-B In equipment requirement) are unmapped despite both being contested. Without the line, 'creates a federal mandate' sweeps in dozens of measures and the key stops meaning anything." Follow-up 0c repeats it as a standing state rather than a one-off: "Rule 3 is now the reason two contested bills stay dark: H.R. 973 (105 member-votes) and S. 2503 (98). Both were re-read in this pass and left where rule 3 put them. If rule 3 is ever revisited, these are the two measures that change." THE DRAFTED ARGUMENT IS THE ONE RULE 3 FORBIDS, ALMOST WORD FOR WORD. It said: the whole bill is an instruction to an agency to promulgate rules under 5 U.S.C. 553, therefore gov_regulation. That is 'the measure directs an agency to issue a rule'. The best version of the case — that the automatic-adoption subsection makes each future revision of a private standard binding unless the Commission objects within 90 days, which is the inverse of 'require review before new ones take effect' — is a genuine strengthening and it is still not enough, because rule 3's test is the measure's PRIMARY OPERATIVE PURPOSE, and the primary operative purpose of H.R. 973 is lithium-ion battery fire safety. The rulemaking is the instrument, not the subject. AND THE MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED RULE 3 RATHER THAN BEATING IT. Projected through the harness the row moves 38 members from a uniform gov_regulation record to a mixed one. That is not a bonus finding, it is rule 3's stated harm in numbers: "it would turn a member's deregulation stance into a contradiction on any safety vote", 38 times, on a suspension vote about battery testing. The wave had written that up as its honest headline before checking the runbook, which is the whole reason a standing-doctrine check has to run before the measurement and not after. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: revisiting rule 3 on its own terms, in a pass that argues the boundary and re-reads every live gov_regulation row against the new line — the runbook already names H.R. 973 and S. 2503 as the two measures that would change. That is a doctrine pass. This wave is a mapping wave and does not have the standing.

questionA_senatePrimaryHoles.whyZero: The 21 candidates split cleanly into two structurally hopeless groups and there is no third group. refusedProposals.rule5_NO_RESTUFFING: FAILS, and this is what makes rule 3's failure fatal. The only way the new key carries more than one instrument is to move H.R. 1005 and H.R. 1049 into it, which rule 5 forbids. Left alone, the key founds on H.R. 1069 by itself — and then it fails rule 1 too.

refusedProposals.verdict: REFUSED on rules 3 and 5, and therefore on rule 1. The fight is real and it is already housed: three instruments, three homes, decided on what each bill's text operatively DOES rather than on the motive they share. H.R. 1069 going to public_schools rather than to a new foreign-influence key is the same discipline applied a third time.

whatShipsThisWave._soWhatIsTheProduct: Four things, none of them a coverage number. (1) A rebuilt census that measures Option A dead rather than asserting it: 21 candidate promotes, +0/-0 each, and a whole-roster proof that all 2806 unread federal rows are structurally unconvertible by any mapping. (2) A complete sweep of the 33-measure unmapped pool with every tally printed, which is the work the next wave does not have to repeat. (3) Two drafted-and-measured rows kept in full beside the standing refusals that block them, so the pass that revisits runbook rule 3 or follow-up 0c starts from an argued draft and a measured cost instead of a blank page. (4) Follow-up 0c's vocabulary question, answered in the negative under the six standing rules — which converts H.R. 1069 from 'unmapped until the vocabulary question is decided' to 'unmapped because it was decided', and that is a smaller claim than a mapping but a more durable one.
whatShipsThisWave._whyNoMigrationWasShipped: A migration was written and then withdrawn, unapplied, in the same session that wrote it. The order of work is the lesson: the rows were drafted from the engrossed text, projected through the harness, and measured clean (+74 clear, 0 lost) BEFORE the standing-doctrine check ran. The measurement was the strongest argument the wave had and it was the wrong argument, because runbook rule 3 predicted the 38-member effect the wave had written up as its honest headline. A doctrine check that runs after the measurement is a doctrine check that argues with a number it has already fallen for. It runs first from now on.

standingWallsFound._why: The brief's walls include 'a promote that does not convert unread rows is a written block, not a mapping' and rule 25's requirement to surface contradictions rather than silently fix them.
